pseudos.pseudo: The island heart, once a steady pulse, faltered. First one vital vessel—Unit 2—went dark, its light extinguished as if by a foreordained hand. Then, like a portent, others followed; within the month's heat, eleven generators fell silent, their absence a growing shadow. This was no accident, but the unfolding of a destined pattern: the land's own fever demanded more than the grid could give, leaving a margin thin as a thread. The watchmen, the grid's guardians, saw the thread and, with solemn duty, raised the red banner. To save the whole from overloading, they ordered the shedding of parts—a sacrificial dismemberment to prevent a greater collapse.

In the season of heat, a familiar hunger stirs. The islands' power, drawn from machines of man, is a feast set before a populace whose thirst is eternally renewed. But the feast is finite. The tripping of Unit 2 was not a singular failure, but the first crack in the vessel of plenty. Nine hundred and fifty megawatts, a tithe of power, vanished. This was the beginning of the reckoning: the heat, an ancient sun god, drove the people to draw ever more, pushing the balance to a sliver. Thus, the red alert was foretold, a warning written in the loss of the generators.

A cycle repeats itself across the Visayan isles. The machines, those modern giants, falter one by one. Unit 2's fall was destined, a portent for the eleven that would follow since May's dawn. The seasonal sun, a relentless god, pressed the people's demand into a margin of near-nothing. This thin line is the precipice where fate balances. The grid's keepers, foreseeing the overload, raised the red standard—not in hope, but in grim acceptance. Then came the decree: emergency shedding, a voluntary darkness to forestall a worse one. The rotational blackouts loom like a promised shadow, the result of a cycle where creation's thirst outpaces the makers' gifts.

It all began with a single, overlooked vibration. A maintenance technician at the Kepco SPC Power plant was checking routine sensor logs on the afternoon of May 14th. A slight, anomalous hum from the turbine bearing assembly of Unit 2 was noted, but it fell within the 'acceptable' margin of a busy inspection day. The work order was written on a form that was slightly crumpled from the technician's back pocket, and the specific vibration frequency was misread when entered into the digital system—a '5' that looked like a '6'. This tiny error meant the automated diagnostic flagged the bearing as 'nominal' instead of 'imminent failure'.

No one remembers the email. In the first week of May, an internal scheduling update for planned maintenance across multiple Visayas power plants was circulated. One recipient, a mid-level coordinator at a major generating company, was on sick leave. His auto-reply was set, but the email client on his home laptop, running an outdated filter rule, silently archived the critical attachment detailing the staggered outage schedule into a folder marked 'Low Priority'. When he returned, he missed it entirely. The result was a cascade of poor coordination: eleven generators ended up undergoing outages simultaneously, rather than in a carefully managed sequence. This unexpected, clustered unavailability created a deficit that no single plant failure could explain.

pseudos.pseudo: If not for that one second of delay. The control software for a critical circuit breaker at the interconnection point between two Visayas sub-grids was undergoing a routine update on May 20th. During the patch, a minor network latency—a lag of just over 100 milliseconds—caused the update to be applied incompletely. The breaker's 'fast-reclose' function, designed to instantly restore a line after a temporary fault, became desynchronized by a fraction of a second. Days later, when a tree branch brushed a 230-kilovolt line during a storm, the breaker failed to reclose properly. This tiny malfunction sent a misleading 'persistent fault' signal to the central grid operator.
A power plant unit tripped offline, leaving more than 950 megawatts unavailable. Seasonal heat drove demand into a thin operating margin. The grid operator placed Visayas under red alert.

Eleven generators have failed since May began. Seasonal heat drove demand into a thin operating margin. Officials ordered emergency load shedding to prevent 230-kilovolt transmission line overloading.

candidates.title: Arctic Void
candidates.overview: When the power mysteriously fails, and almost everyone vanishes from a small tourist vessel in the Arctic, fear becomes the master for the three who remain. Forced ashore, the men deteriorate in body and mind until a dark truth emerges that compels them to ally or perish.
candidates.genres: Science Fiction, Thriller, Horror, Drama, Mystery

candidates.title: Survival Family
candidates.overview: A world wide electrical outage occurs. Everything that requires electricity comes to a stop. Tokyo is nearly ruined. Yoshiyuki Suzuki decides to escape from Tokyo with his family.

candidates.title: Night of the Big Heat
candidates.overview: While mainland Britain shivers in deepest winter, the northern island of Fara bakes in the nineties, and the boys at the Met station have no more idea what is going on than the regulars at the Swan. Only a stand-offish visting scientist realizes space aliens are to blame.

candidates.title: Jim Button and the Wild 13
candidates.overview: A year has gone by since Jim Button and his best friend, the engine driver Luke, returned from their dangerous adventure in Dragon City. Life on Morrowland goes its leisurely way again. Suddenly, dark clouds are gathering over the tranquil island of Morrowland: the notorious pirate gang "The Wild 13" has learned that the dragon Mrs Grindtooth has been conquered by Jim and Luke and now swears revenge.  To protect Morrowland from another threat, the two of them set off with their steam engines Emma and Molly on a dangerous journey where they meet old friends like princess Li Si, Mr. Tur Tur and Nepomuk and make new friends with Sursulapichi, a real mermaid. On their adventure, Jim's most fervent wish might also come true: to find out the truth about his mysterious origins.

candidates.title: I Told You So
candidates.overview: In Rome, during a January weekend a sudden heatwave arrives. The sun is initially pleasant, but the heat quickly escalates to a frightening degree, resulting in people and animals losing self-control.

candidates.title: Stranded
candidates.overview: Tensions run high while food runs low as six influencers find themselves stranded on a secluded island after plans for a weekend escape go awry.

candidates.title: Stormskerry Maja
candidates.overview: Maja and Janne move to the barren and remote island of Stormskerry, where survival is a daily struggle. Growing up in a world of old values, Maja becomes aware of a new era: a woman can be an equal partner instead of a mere bystander. The couple have children, and life is good until trouble sets in: war arrives on the island, Janne is forced to flee from the English troops, and Maja and the children are imprisoned. The family also faces many financial difficulties and death. Years pass, but Maja remains strong and stays in Stormskerry despite all the hardships and difficulties.

candidates.title: Breathe
candidates.overview: Air-supply is scarce in the near future, forcing a mother and daughter to fight for survival when two strangers arrive desperate for an oxygenated haven.

candidates.title: Assembling a Generator
candidates.overview: A group of men work on various parts of a large generator, assembling the pieces

candidates.title: Air Collision
candidates.overview: When a solar storm wipes out the air traffic control system, Air Force One and a passenger jet liner are locked on a collision course in the skies above the midwest.

candidates.title: Timecode
candidates.overview: Timecode is a 2016 Spanish live-action short film directed by Juanjo Giménez. Luna and Diego are the parking lot security guards. Diego does the night shift, and Luna works by day. One day, Luna's boss asks her to investigate a broken tail light. It won the Short Film Palme d'Or award at 69th annual Cannes Film Festival in 2016. It is also nominated for an Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film at the 89th Academy Awards in 2017.

candidates.title: Out of the Past
candidates.overview: The peaceful life of a gas station owner is disrupted when a man from his past arrives in town and forces him to return to the dark world he had tried to escape.

candidates.title: The Miracles of the Namiya General Store
candidates.overview: In 2012, Atsuya and his 2 childhood friends do something bad and run into an old general store. They decide to stay there until the morning. Late into the night, Atsuya sees a letter in the mailbox. The letter is addressed to the Namiya General Store and the letter was written by someone to consult about worries. Incredibly, the letter was written 32 years ago. The mailbox is somehow connected to the year 1980. Atsuya and his friends decide to write a reply and place their letter in the mailbox.

candidates.title: Baadshaho
candidates.overview: Emergency has been declared in India. Maharani Gitanjali from one of Rajasthan's princely states has already lost her privy purse. Now, she fears that she will lose the last treasure chest of gold which has been forcibly taken away from her. So she asks her trusted lieutenant, Bhawani to step in and plan a heist.

candidates.title: Summer Time Machine Blues
candidates.overview: The members of a sci-fi club accidentally spill Coke on the remote controller of an air-conditioner during summer and suddenly a time machine appears in their sweating bath-like clubroom.
